changes.before: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
changes.after: In light of the progress on inflation and the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.

changes.before: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
changes.after: The Committee has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent, and judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.

changes.before: In considering any adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate
changes.after: In considering additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate

changes.before: Inflation has eased over the past year but remains somewhat elevated. In recent months, there has been some further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective.
changes.after: Inflation has made further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective but remains somewhat elevated.

changes.before: The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.
changes.after: The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.
Voting against this action was Michelle W. Bowman, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

parsed.rationale: The Committee shifted from holding rates to an outsized 50 bp cut, removed the 'greater confidence' precondition, and signaled additional adjustments, a clear dovish change in policy direction. A hawkish dissent favoring only 25 bp slightly tempers the move but does not change its direction.

spans.quote: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
In considering any adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate
Inflation has eased over the past year but remains somewhat elevated. In recent months, there has been some further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.
In light of the progress on inflation and the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.
The Committee has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent, and judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.
In considering additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate
Inflation has made further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective but remains somewhat elevated.
The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.
Voting against this action was Michelle W. Bowman, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.
